newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DUTCH SOCCER BOARD RESIGNS OVER TV RIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH SOCCER BOARD RESIGNS OVER TV RIGHTS.

text.p: The board of the Dutch soccer association (KNVB) resigned on Wednesday as the row continued over the sale of exclusive television rights to failed Dutch sports channel Sport7.

The board decided on Friday to step down but were asked by 34 of the 36 professional soccer clubs to stay on despite the closure of Sport7, plagued by poor viewing figures and wrangles over broadcasting rights.
The station, in which the KNVB has a stake, racked up losses of least 100 million guilders in its brief four-month existence.

The KNVB sold exclusive rights for Dutch league soccer to Sport7 in a seven-year deal worth over one billion guilders. But the association's entitlement to this was then challenged by in the courts by league heavywieghts Feyenoord Rotterdam and Ajax Amsterdam.
KNVB chairman Jos Staatsen had indicated the board would resign if it did not have the backing from all clubs to change regulations and allow it to sell all television rights, including live matches.

Ajax Amsterdam and Feyenoord oppose such changes, believing they own the rights for home matches and would go no further than giving the KNVB permission to sell rights on highlights, with the home teams able to negotiate separately on live matches.
